Chimichurri Poached Chicken

SERVES

PREP
TIME

DAIRY-FREE, EGG-FREE

@ We keep a jar of Chimichurri (page 32) in the door of the fridge, and it makes an, easy,
sharp finish, for anything off the grill, roast potatoes, a fried egg,
and here, chicken. Bone-in thighs work too if you'd like, by heck
them with a thermometer a little later than you would when cooking
chicken breasts.

= 1% pounds boneless,
skinless chicken breasts,
cut into 6 pieces

1 leek, halved

1 celery stalk, halved

2 onion, halved

2 garlic cloves, smashed

3 sprigs fresh oregano
or marjoram

1 cup Chimichurri
(page 32)

2 tablespoons
chopped fresh curly
parsley

Va teaspoon freshly
ground black pepper

Per Serving Calories: 241;
Total Fat: 12g; Saturated Fat:
2g; Cholesterol: 68mg; Sodium:
310mg; Total Carbohydrates: 5g;
Fiber: 1g; Protein: 29g

1. Lay the chicken in a deep saucepan. Fij|
with cold water until it’s about one inch over
the top of the chicken. Add the leek, celery, onion.
garlic, and oregano. Cover and bring it just to a simmer.
Drop the heat to low (keeping the lid on), and
poach for 12 to 15 minutes, or until a thermometer in the thickest
piece of the chicken shows 165°F and the
meat has turned opaque.

2. Lift the chicken out of the pan and let it rest

for 5 minutes.

3. When you're ready to eat, spoon % cup of
chimichurri over a warm platter.
Slice the chicken, lay it on top, and spoon
over the rest of the sauce. Finish the
platter with parsley and pepper.

Prep tip: Poaching chicken breasts in barely moving water
keeps them tender. Save the pan liquid for
a quick noodle soup the next day; it makes a decent light
chicken broth once you have strained out the vegetables.
